scope: Bounded structural context only; no political-outcome assessment.

facts.source: 2019 Constitution of Republic of Cuba, WIPO Lex-hosted Spanish PDF; PDF marked Gaceta Oficial 10 Apr 2019
facts.fact: Article 5 names the PCC the superior political guiding force of society and the State. Article 128(i)-(j) assigns the President supreme leadership of armed institutions, organization, and chairing the National Defense Council. Article 220 defines state armed institutions as the Revolutionary Armed Forces and armed formations of the Interior Ministry. Constitutional text does not prove de facto command, elite cohesion or obedience in 2026.

facts.source: Current official 2026 UN records reused from linked parent
facts.fact: The 29 Sep UN General Assembly President readout identifies Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla as Cuba’s serving Foreign Affairs Minister and records his meeting with PGA Khalilur Rahman. The 1 Oct UN in Cuba story documents coordination among science agencies, Civil Defense and provincial/municipal governments. See exact receipts in parent addendum.

facts.source: White House presidential remarks at UN General Assembly, 22 Sep 2026
facts.fact: President Trump stated broadly that the U.S. would use military power in the Western Hemisphere if needed to protect U.S. interests and said freedom would come to Cuba. The page is a public policy/intent statement; it contains no Cuba-specific deployment order, operation date or troop-movement report.

limits: Constitution copy captured is the April 2019 text; official Cuban Gazette PDF request timed out. No consolidated version incorporating later changes verified; do not assume provisions unchanged.

No current independent evidence of military/elite cohesion, actual command obedience, defections or current U.S. force posture/deployment was captured. White House rhetoric does not establish military action or timetable.
